div.div:
Empirical partition
Latent heat from available energy via the Priestley–Taylor coefficient αPT.
Sensible heat is the complement.

div.div:
Partition closure
LEPT = αPT · f(Rn − G)
HPT = (Rn − G) − LEPT
Balance closes by construction:
RE ≈ 0.

Gradient-ratio estimate
Latent and sensible heat from temperature and moisture gradients via Bowen ratio β, with stability corrections.

div.div:
Partition closure
H = β / (1 + β) · (Rn − G)
LE = 1 / (1 + β) · (Rn − G)
If β is finite and valid, balance closes:
RE ≈ 0.

Aerodynamic–energy approach for latent heat
Latent heat estimated from available energy and an aerodynamic drying-power term.
No sensible heat is calculated.

No paired closure
Open complement after subtracting latent heat:
UPenman = Rn − G − LEPenman
Not automatically sensible heat.

div.div:
Rn: net radiation (W m−2) G: soil heat flux (W m−2) H: sensible heat flux (W m−2) LE: latent heat flux (W m−2) RE = Rn − G − H − LE
Bulk–Residual combines two levels. First, Hbulk is estimated using a temperature gradient and an exchange-velocity scale. This scale may be a simple mean-wind approximation (wind_mean), a profile-derived friction velocity from two wind heights (u_star_profile), or a roughness-based friction velocity (u_star_roughness). This makes the sensible-heat estimate more or less close to a neutral profile-transfer logic. Second, latent heat is calculated as the residual of the available energy: LEres = Rn − G − Hbulk. A near-zero closure residual therefore confirms the algebraic residual construction. It does not prove that the selected exchange-velocity assumption is physically correct.
Monin–Obukhov / Profile does not normalize fluxes to available energy. The residual RM is diagnostic and must not be forced to zero.
Penman provides only latent heat. The open complement UPenman is not automatically sensible heat.

switch.text: Rn: net radiation (W m−2) G: soil heat flux (W m−2) H: sensible heat flux (W m−2) LE: latent heat flux (W m−2) RE = Rn − G − H − LE...
